Q: What is the equivalent Cmd.exe program for this PowerShell one-liner program? A:

Dissect the following PowerShell command:

Get-ChildItem -Path E:\input\ -Include *.xml | foreach { $html="E:\output\"+$_.basename+".html"; .\program $_.fullname $html}
  • Get-ChildItem -Path E:\input\ gets all the items under folder E:\input
  • -Include *.xml match the files with file name extension .xml
  • foreach { ... } applies the list to a loop, in each iteration the file object will be represented as $_
  • $html="E:\output\"+$_.basename+".html" for each found XML file, constructs a file path with .xml replaced by .html
  • .\program $_.fullname $html runs a program with 2 arguments: original .xml file path and the new .html file path

It is actually do-able in cmd.exe execept that it needs to loop / iterate directly on the folder, the rest can be achieved from there.

  • Use the for %%f in (PATH\PATTERN) do SOME_COMMAND syntax to loop over a given PATH and the files matching the PATTERN. Each matched item in the iteration is represented as %%f. Since you only want to scan for .xml files in E:\input folder, the command would be for %%f in (E:\input\*.xml) do SOME_COMMAND. The letter f is chosen arbitrarily, which stands for "file".
  • For SOME_COMMAND, we can simply use %%f to represent the original .xml file path. But to get the file path with an .html file name extension, we need to use the %%~nf.html syntax to get the base file name (%%~nf) with .html appended. Then we need to prepend E:\input\ to form the full path. So, it would be .\program %%f E:\input\%%~nf.html
  • There is a possibility that some file names could contain spaces. To cope with that, just quote the paths with a pair of double quotes " "
  • Add that to a .bat file. Need to add a @echo off to prevent it from showing the script file content.

The translated cmd.exe Batch script file is like this:

@echo off

for %%f in (E:\input\*.xml) do .\program "%%f" "E:\input\%%~nf.html"

You can also use the for ... in (...) do (\n...\n) syntax to improve readability:

@echo off

for %%f in (E:\input\*.xml) do (
    .\program "%%f" "E:\input\%%~nf.html"
)

See also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/for

Q: How to run Powershell on a list of computers (get-wmiobject SoftwareLicensingProduct) A:

Assuming remote powershell or wsman is enabled. For get-wmiobject, you would need the dcom port available. Computername can be an array. Using a wmi filter is 30 seconds faster thanks to partialProductKey.

enum LicenseStatus {
  Unlicensed
  Licensed
  OOBGrace
  OOTGrace
  NonGenuineGrace
  Notification
  ExtendedGrace
}
$computers = Get-Content computers.txt
$filter = "partialProductKey is not null and 
  applicationid = '55c92734-d682-4d71-983e-d6ec3f16059f'"
Get-ciminstance SoftwareLicensingProduct -ComputerName $computers -filter $filter |
  select PartialProductKey, Description, ProductKeyChannel, 
  @{n='licensestatus'; e={[licensestatus]$_.licensestatus}},
  pscomputername

PartialProductKey : 2YT43
Description       : Windows(R) Operating System, VOLUME_KMSCLIENT channel
ProductKeyChannel : Volume:GVLK
licensestatus     : Licensed
PSComputerName    : localhost

Q: Use of the checkSelfPermission in Android? A:

On my app's user preferences screen, I show a dialog and call requestPermissions when the user enables the bluetooth features.

I use checkSelfPermissions to verify the permissions are still granted before the bluetooth scans, since the user could enable the feature in user preferences, but then revoke the permission from the system's appInfo screen. If I didn't do this, the app would crash since the preference option said to run them, but the app permissions are denied.

Q: adding text decorations to console output A:

Just for future viewers, the API calls are not needed anymore under later .NET versions.

The following in .NET 4.8 works perfectly as is, no extern required.

const string CLS ="\u001bc\x1b[3J";         //clear screen
const string RESET = "\x1B[0m";             //set format to default
const string BOLD = "\x1B[1m";              //bold text
const string DISABLED = "\x1B[2m";          //darkens, based on color
const string ITALICS = "\x1B[3m";           //italics text
const string UNDERLINE = "\x1B[4m";         //underline text
const string BLINK = "\x1B[5m";             //blinks from set color to darker set color.
const string INVERT = "\x1B[7m";            //inverts background with foreground.
const string STRIKE = "\x1B[9m";            //strikethrough the text
const string FGCOLOR = "\u001b[38;5;3m";    //38 - foreground, 3m - yellow (256 color palette)
const string BGCOLOR = "\u001b[48;5;1m";    //48 - background, 1m - red (256 color palette)

/*
EDIT: Note, you can get (24bit color palette) with slight adjustment.
                                  R  ;G  ;B
const string FGCOLOR = "\u001b[38;255;255;0m"; //38 - foreground yellow
                                  R  ;G;B
const string BGCOLOR = "\u001b[48;255;0;0m";   //48 - background red 
*/

Console.WriteLine($"{CLS}Demo: " +
                    $"{UNDERLINE}underlined{RESET}, " +
                    $"{FGCOLOR}{ITALICS}ITALICS{RESET}, " +
                    $"{FGCOLOR}{DISABLED}DISABLED{RESET}, " +
                    $"{BOLD}BOLD{RESET}, " +
                    $"{BLINK}BLINK{RESET}, " +
                    $"{FGCOLOR}FGCOLOR, " +
                    $"{INVERT}INVERT{RESET}, " +
                    $"{BGCOLOR}BGCOLOR, " +
                    $"{INVERT}INVERT{RESET}, " +
                    $"{STRIKE}STRIKE{RESET} " +
                    $"text.");

Q: How to Create SSH Key in git A:

Using SSH (Secure Shell) instead of https seems the Secure & Fastest method. Just providing few links and tips here to make things a bit easy. You can check this step-by-step guide! provided by docs.github to "Check existing SSH keys, Generate, Add a new SSH key to your GitHub account, and more."

Tip #1: During the process you need to confirm SSH key fingerprints to validate the connection. Compare the key of the algorithm you chose respectively (RSA, ECDSA, or Ed25519) and confirm it. Check this link to compare the key: GitHub's public key fingerprints!

Tip #2: If you don't want to type passphrase every time you push, just press enter when it prompts to choose passphrase.

CAUTION: Other methods using https $ git config credential.helper store etc., even with using 'timeout' might seem faster but are 100% unencrypted and hence not secure. However, you can encrypt that config file and just decrypt it before use, but there is still a chance we might forget to encrypt it again after use. You can use it at your discretion.
